summary: Ryoichi Kondo worked in Buddhist studies. His posts include professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. By 2026, he held positions as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryojin Soga was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Shinshu and Otani universities and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He served as a professor at Toyo University (1916–1924) and as a professor and 17th president at Otani University.
Ryojun Mitomo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held professorships at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).
Ryokei Kaginushi was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University, with his tenure in the Faculty of Letters attested in 1978 and as professor in 1993.

Ryoken Nawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. Affiliations include commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2026).

Ryoko Mochizuki is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1958 to 1963. Mochizuki served as a lecturer at Rissho University around 1968 and 1980.

Ryosaburo Sakaki worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, having studied at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Ryukoku University (1897), the Third Higher School (1899), and Kyoto University (professor, 1908).

Ryosei Fukuda, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Toyo University. He became a professor at Taisho University in 1973 (emeritus in 2007) and held head posts at Chisan Denpōin, Chisan Kangakukai, and Chisan Senshu Gakuin.

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. Nakao served as a professor (attested 1998) and later professor emeritus (attested 2026) at Hanazono University, and was a member of Soto-shu Shumu Kenkyujo.

Ryosho Hayashi specialized in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, studying at Taisho and Tokyo Metropolitan universities. He served as professor (1975), dean of literature (1981), and professor emeritus (1990–1994) at Taisho University.

Ryosho Nakamura is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Ensho Kanakura, at Seventh Higher School Zoshikan, Tohoku University, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at The International University of Kagoshima from around 1956 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. He served Komazawa University as professor (1964), dean (1991), emeritus professor (2003), and president (2009), and was also a professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Koda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology and studied under Seitatsu Matsunami. Koda held researcher positions at Taisho University (attested 1998) and the Hasegawa Institute for Buddhist Culture (attested 2006).

Ryoshu Michihata, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied at Otani University (~1924–1928). He held a post at Otani University (~1934–1969) and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University (~1969–1978).
Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1942 to 1948. Misaki later served as an emeritus professor at Waseda University from around 1988 to 2010.

Ryoshun Okubo, a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar, studied at Waseda University (~1973–1983). Okubo served as Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism at Waseda University (~1997) and held professorships at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and ICPBS (attested 2026).

Ryudo Fujii studied Indology and philosophy under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson. Fujii's career includes posts at JSPS (attested 2003), Kokushikan University (attested 2010), and Kyoto Women's University (attested 2015).

Ryugen Tanemura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Tanemura's posts include part-time lecturer at Nishogakusha University (attested 2013), researcher at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute (attested 2014), and faculty at Taisho University (attested 2014–2026).

Ryuhiko Taga studied at Rissho University (~1953–1955) in the field of Buddhist studies. Taga had a long career at Rissho University as lecturer (~1958–1965), associate professor (~1965–1975), professor (~1975–2001), and president (~1992–1998).
